newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES UP DESPITE LIQUIDITY.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES UP DESPITE LIQUIDITY.

text.p: Short-term trading rates on Zimbabwe's money market were indicated up on Friday despite improved liquidity.

"The market is very quiet and I think rates are likely to go up because there are no maturities. We are trying to sell but no-one wants to buy so we are indicating higher buying rates to cover our position," one dealer said.
The dealers said the benchmark treasury bill rate edged lower to 20.19 percent at Thursday's weekly auction from 20.21 percent.

NCD bills maturing after 30, 60 and 90 days were being bought at 27 percent and sold at 22 percent, up from 23 and 22 percent overnight while the buying rate for bankers' acceptance bills was indicated at 24 percent and selling at 21 percent from 22.75 percent and 22 percent.
Call money eased to 20 percent from 23 percent with the central Reserve Bank indicating a market surplus of Z$77.8 million compared to Thursday's Z$50 million deficit.
